IWG opens two flexible workspaces in Bugis, expands Singapore network to 25 centres
article:
International Workplace Group (IWG) has opened two flexible workspaces in the Bugis area — OpenOffice Fortune Centre and HQ Liang Seah — bringing its Singapore network to 25 centres across six brands.

The two openings also mark the Singapore debut of IWG’s OpenOffice and HQ brands. Both centres offer co-working spaces, private offices and meeting rooms.

OpenOffice Fortune Centre is located within the 20-storey mixed-use Fortune Centre in the Bras Basah-Bugis precinct. The centre comprises 17 workstations, five private offices and a meeting room, catering to companies ranging from startups to established firms.

The workspace is within walking distance of five MRT stations — Bencoolen, Rochor, Bras Basah, Bugis and Dhoby Ghaut. Orchard Road and the CBD are about a 10-minute drive away.

OpenOffice operates with a low-staffing model supported by technology-enabled, self-service workspaces. Previously available in Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong, the brand’s Singapore debut also marks its first entry into Southeast Asia.

Meanwhile, HQ Liang Seah is located within a traditional shophouse at 1 Liang Seah Street. The centre offers 70 workstations, 18 private offices and three meeting rooms.

The property is surrounded by restaurants and retail amenities in the Bugis area, and is within walking distance of Bugis, City Hall and Esplanade MRT stations.

The two centres bring IWG’s portfolio in Singapore to 25 locations under six brands: Regus, Signature, Spaces, No.18, OpenOffice and HQ.

Vijayakumar Tangarasan, IWG’s country head for Singapore, Malaysia and Brunei, said the new centres reflect growing demand for flexible workspaces in Singapore.

He added that the group is expanding across different locations, including the CBD, city-fringe areas and decentralised locations closer to residential neighbourhoods, to cater to companies looking to establish or grow their presence in Singapore.

The Singapore openings come amid IWG’s wider expansion globally. The group signed 728 new locations worldwide in 1H2026, bringing its network to more than 6,000 signed locations across over 120 countries.

IWG said 95% of its new locations are being delivered through managed partnership agreements with property owners and investors.

Christian Schmitz, CEO of IWG, said demand for flexible and platform working is growing as more companies adopt hybrid working arrangements and seek greater flexibility in their office footprint.

In 2025, IWG signed 1,132 new locations globally, of which 99% were partnership agreements.

title: IOI Properties to acquire Lee Yeow Seng’s Shenton House vehicle for $1
article:
Malaysia-listed IOI Properties Group (IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101, the private vehicle owned by its group CEO and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng that holds Shenton House , for a nominal $1.

Under the conditional agreement announced on Oct 1, IOIPG will also settle about $217.6 million in shareholder advances that Lee had injected into Shenton 101. Upon completion, the company will consolidate Shenton 101’s borrowings of about $376.23 million into its accounts. Both amounts were as at July 31, 2026.

The transaction reverses the August 2024 decision, when IOIPG’s non-interested directors rejected an earlier proposal by Lee to sell Shenton 101 to the group, citing its heavy capital commitments at the time.

Lee had acquired Shenton House in his personal capacity through Shenton 101 for $538 million in a collective sale tender in November 2023. The acquisition was completed in June 2024.

IOIPG said Lee had originally proposed transferring the property to the group to avoid a potential conflict of interest. Following the 2024 rejection, IOIPG instead entered into project and property management agreements to manage Shenton House and its redevelopment without holding any economic interest in the property.

Why IOI Properties revisited the deal

The group said it is revisiting the acquisition at Lee’s request as its “circumstances and strategic position have evolved”.

IOI Central Boulevard Towers has since achieved committed occupancy of more than 95% and is self-sustaining in terms of debt servicing. IOIPG has also completed the acquisition of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties, which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach, as well as Asia Square Tower 2 .

IOIPG said acquiring Shenton 101 would strengthen its presence in the Marina Bay precinct and allow it to benefit from the redevelopment’s potential profits and capital appreciation. Shenton House is within walking distance of IOI Central Boulevard Towers and Asia Square Tower 2.

Source: EdgeProp Landlens

$1.61 bil Shenton House redevelopment

The existing 25-storey strata-titled commercial building at 3 Shenton Way sits on a 36,350 sq ft site. It is zoned commercial with a gross plot ratio of 11.2 under the 2019 Master Plan and has a 99-year lease from June 1969, leaving about 42 years remaining.

Under the CBD Incentive Scheme, the site is eligible for a 25% bonus gross floor area, allowing a maximum gross plot ratio of 14.0 for a commercial and hotel redevelopment.

IOIPG plans to redevelop the property into a 35-storey mixed-use development comprising 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 165-room luxury hotel spanning 10 floors, a retail basement and three carpark levels, along with sky terraces, restaurants and a swimming pool.

The redevelopment would increase the property’s net lettable area from 218,246 sq ft to about 393,185 sq ft. The underlying land tenure is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year lease, subject to the requisite approvals and payment of a lease renewal premium.

Savills valued Shenton House as a redevelopment site at $585 million as at Aug 15, after deducting the land betterment charge and lease renewal premium. The proposed redevelopment has an estimated gross development value of $1.61 billion, with redevelopment costs estimated at $973.65 million.

URA granted provisional permission for the redevelopment on June 8, although written permission remains outstanding. Construction is expected to begin in 1H2027 and be completed in 4Q2031, subject to approvals.

The acquisition will be funded from IOIPG’s internally generated funds. It does not require approval from non-interested shareholders as its transaction ratio of 3.79% is below the 5% threshold under Bursa Malaysia’s listing rules.

Lee and his brother, Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is also deemed interested in the transaction, abstained and will continue to abstain from board deliberations and voting on the proposal.

Completion, targeted for 4Q2026, remains subject to several conditions, including approval from Bank Negara Malaysia for investment in foreign-currency assets beyond the group’s permissible limit, consent from Shenton 101’s lenders and the Singapore Land Authority, and a waiver of a right of first refusal held by Multi Wealth (Singapore) and its related companies.

title: Bargain or Trap? 3 Worst-Performing SGX Blue Chips in Q3 2026
article:
The third quarter of 2026 rewarded investors who simply owned the market.
The
SPDR STI ETF
(SGX: ES3), which tracks Singapore’s
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI), returned 11.6% for the quarter.
Three
blue chips
went the other way.
DFI Retail Group
(SGX: D01) delivered a total return of negative 13.1%.
UOL Group
(SGX: U14) and
SATS
(SGX: S58) did slightly worse, at negative 13.3% and negative 13.6%, respectively.
Even after counting dividends, each stock trailed the index by about 25 percentage points.
The odd part is that all three grew their profits in their latest results.
Their cash flow, however, told a weaker story.
For income investors, that gap matters – because
free cash flow
is the lifeblood of dividends.
Why would a bigger dividend disappoint DFI investors?
DFI
runs 7,659 outlets across 12 markets under familiar brands like Guardian, 7-Eleven and IKEA.
In the first half of 2026 (1H2026), revenue fell 6% year on year (YoY) to US$4.1 billion.
There is context behind that dip: the drop stemmed from selling the Singapore Food business and closing Mannings China.
Strip those out, and underlying subsidiary revenue from continuing businesses actually grew 4%.
Profits also moved in the right direction.
Underlying profit attributable to shareholders rose 11% YoY to US$117 million (up 44% on a continuing-business basis).
Meanwhile, free cash flow dipped 9.3% to US$382.7 million as DFI spent more on capital expenditure.
The dividend is where things got awkward:
Interim ordinary dividend: US$0.062, up 77% from US$0.035
Special dividend:
Nil, compared with US$0.443 a year ago
While the ordinary dividend grew, the total cheque shrank significantly.
Shareholders anchoring on last year’s special payout will collect far less this time, and the market may still be adjusting to that reset.
The bargain case rests on the balance sheet.
DFI held net debt of just US$22 million as at 30 June 2026, and management raised its full-year underlying profit guidance to between US$285 million and US$305 million.
Where did UOL’s cash go?
UOL develops homes and commercial properties and owns hotels under the Pan Pacific and PARKROYAL brands.
Its revenue fell 7% YoY to S$1.4 billion in 1H2026.
So where did the revenue go? Into joint ventures, mostly.
UOL has structured projects such as PARKTOWN Residence and Skye at Holland as JVs.
AMO Residence also stopped contributing after it obtained its temporary occupation permit in October 2025.
The profits followed.
UOL’s share of joint venture profits rose by S$83.7 million YoY, pushing profit before fair value gains and income tax up 17% to S$373.1 million.
Cash flow tells a different story.
Free cash flow swung to negative S$129.8 million from positive S$317.6 million a year ago, driven by a S$298.1 million outflow for the Dorset Road site acquisition and development costs.
Net gearing rose to 0.26 times, up from 0.20 times at 31 December 2025.
Shareholders shouldn’t expect an interim payout – UOL typically pays dividends once a year, having distributed S$0.25 per share for FY2025 in May 2026.
Look past the land purchase, and the picture improves.
Net asset value per share rose to S$14.20 from S$13.92.
Management expects Singapore’s residential market to stay firm and sees offices keeping their momentum, as supply in the central business district stays tight.
Can SATS grow faster than its costs?
SATS handles air cargo and runs large central kitchens for airlines and institutions, across more than 225 stations in 27 countries.
Reporting quarterly, SATS latest figures cover the three months ended 30 June 2026 (1QFY2027).
On the surface, growth looked strong.
Revenue rose 11.3% YoY to S$1.7 billion, while cargo volume processed grew 8.6% to 2.6 million tonnes, outpacing IATA’s benchmarks.
Non-aviation meal volumes also grew by 20%.
The catch? Profits didn’t keep pace.
Operating margin narrowed to 8.0% from 8.3%, as Middle East disruptions and inflation hurt efficiency.
Associate and joint venture earnings fell 18.9%, leaving net profit up just 6% to S$75.1 million.
Cash flow fell further behind.
Operating cash flow after lease repayments dropped to S$23.2 million from S$45.8 million, which SATS attributed to working capital timing.
Free cash flow came in at negative S$22.6 million.
Total debt stood at S$4.2 billion, with gross debt-to-equity ratio holding steady at 1.4 times.
As was the case a year ago, SATS declared no quarterly dividend.
Management sounded cautious, warning that
higher oil prices
and Middle East tensions could weigh more heavily in the coming quarters.
Get Smart: Follow the cash, not the headline
When profits rise but a share price falls, follow the cash.
Cash spent on future projects is not the same as cash that never showed up.
UOL put its cash into a new development site, while DFI still generated a healthy US$382.7 million in free cash flow.
SATS faces the toughest test, with negative free cash flow and persistent operational headwinds.
So, bargain or trap?
Wait for the next set of results before you decide.
If free cash flow starts catching up with profits, the sell-off may have gone too far.
If it doesn’t, the lower price may be telling you something about the dividend.
If the market falls further, will you be ready… or fully invested?

title: Glencore expects its commodity-trading profits to top US$5 bil this year
article:
(Oct 2): Glencore plc expects its commodity-trading profits to exceed US$5 billion ($6.4 billion) this year, putting it on track for one of the best results in its history.

The bumper haul has primarily been driven by “the materially reshaped crude oil, refined products, gas and freight markets”, the trading house said in a statement on Friday.

A US$5 billion profit would be Glencore’s best result since its 2022 record, when energy markets were rocked by Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2026, traders are again reaping huge earnings as the Iran war fuels wild energy price swings and major dislocations between regional markets. Freight costs have also surged on the back of disruptions to flows through the Strait of Hormuz, while rising copper and coal prices have been an additional boon to Glencore.

Shares in the London-listed trader and miner jumped as much as 2.8%, reflecting the near-term forecast as well as higher long-term pre-tax earnings guidance. From 2027, Glencore expects the marketing division to bring in about US$2.8 billion to US$4.2 billion annually.

See also: Super El Niño set to turn sugar glut to deficit this season

The company has consistently beaten its long-term profit targets in recent years, fuelled mainly by “movements in commodity prices, inflation, the commercial opportunity set and our overall business volumes and scale”, it said. In August, it reported overall core earnings of US$10.1 billion for the first half, 86% higher than a year earlier.

title: CDL shares end week nearly 15% lower, erasing over $1 bil in market cap
article:
City Developments (CDL) shares ended the week more than 14% lower than it began. Closing at $7.04 on Oct 2, CDL shares are near levels last seen in October 2025 and close to the stock’s 52-week low of $6.87.

The property group has lost over $1 billion in market capitalisation in the five trading days after a new plan was unveiled to divest $6 billion of assets while deploying $5 billion into Singapore, China and Japan.

CDL shares fell more than 8% to a two-month low over Sept 28, the day of the announcement.

The outcome of CDL’s year-long strategic review, spearheaded by Teneo, broadly outlines plans to divest mainly commercial and hospitality properties in the UK, China and Australia.

The group is pulling out of Down Under. CDL is “planning to do an orderly exit of nearly all of our presence there, except for hospitality”, says CDL group CEO Sherman Kwek at a briefing on Sept 28.

Kwek says CDL has been “unable to build scale”, and Australia “is not a market that has really worked out too well for us”.

See also: Is this why CDL was sold down after its strategic review?

CDL also shared a 60%-30%-10% breakdown for its $5 billion of new investments across Singapore, China and Japan. This comes despite CDL’s pandemic-era misadventure in China, where it recorded a $1.78 bil impairment on Sincere Property Group in FY2020 ended Dec 31, 2020.

Kwek sought to assuage investors, saying: “Yes, I know when you put China there, everyone’s spooked. But we have to look at our business in the longer term, and I always believe in the value of being a well-diversified company. It’s not good just to be exposed and fully concentrated in one market, no matter how strong you are in that market.”

China’s real estate market “is not in good shape” and is “under tremendous pressure”, admits Kwek. That said, there are still opportunities in the market, he adds.

See also: PLUS points: What’s in CDL’s three-year roadmap?

CDL also plans to “optimise” its global hospitality portfolio of 165 hotels with around 47,795 rooms, including 88 owned hotels.

It will sort its owned hotels into three buckets. CDL says it will retain some $5 billion worth of core, “well-performing” assets but targets to divest approximately $1.8 billion of mature, non-core or underperforming assets through FY2029, representing 30% of its $6 billion divestment target.

The remaining $1.8 billion in hospitality assets will be put through asset enhancement initiatives or redevelopment before CDL decides whether to divest or recognise them as core holdings.

Finally, the group wants to focus on fund management. Kwek says CDL will establish a dedicated fund management entity, as the group aims to double AUM from $5 billion as of June 30 to $10 billion by FY2029. The group also plans to hire a dedicated CEO and management team, formalising what is currently an in-house operation.

Shares in CDL fell 1.1% over Oct 2 to close at $7.04, down 12.2% year to date.

Is this why CDL was sold down after its strategic review?

title: JP Morgan Singapore & Asia Equity Income Fund surpasses $1 bil AUM in eight months
article:
The JP Morgan Singapore & Asia Equity Income Fund has reached $1.26 billion AUM as of Aug 31, shares JP Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) in an announcement. The fund was launched in January under the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS) Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP) and is available to retail, accredited and institutional investors in Singapore.

Seeking to deliver diversified income with competitive total returns through combining an actively managed, income-oriented portfolio of Singapore and Asian equities with a disciplined options overlay strategy, the fund is managed by Singapore-based equity portfolio managers Pauline Ng and Changqi Ong. They are supported by a seasoned team with over 15 years of proven expertise in generating alpha across ASEAN equity and Asian income strategies, as well as a dedicated derivative group headed by Stuart O’Neill.

Ayaz Ebrahim, CEO of Singapore, South East Asia, and India at JPMAM, says that crossing $1 billion in AUM is an important milestone for the fund and the firm’s business. “As the first global manager appointed under the EQDP initiative, we are proud to support the continued deepening of Singapore’s equity market while bringing investors a differentiated income solution, one that combines active equity investing with our options overlay expertise,” he remarks. “Reaching this milestone reflects the strong investor demand we have seen for the strategy and Singapore's growing role as a gateway to Asia.”

From left: Ayaz Ebrahim, Gidon Jerome Kessel (group head, deposit and wealth management, UOB), Paul Bateman (chairman, JPMAM), Yao Loong Ng (head of global financial markets, SGX), Wai Mei Hong and Paul Thompson (head of Singapore and Southeast Asia, JP Morgan Private Bank). Photo: JPMAM

JP Morgan remains committed to working with the Singapore government agencies and players across the ecosystem to help strengthen market resilience and sustain Singapore’s role as a key gateway to Asia, shares Wai Mei Hong, senior country officer at JP Morgan Singapore. She adds: “Singapore’s strength as a financial hub is built on trust and a culture of long-term partnership across the industry. We are proud to contribute to the continued vibrancy of the local capital markets by bringing global investment expertise and solutions that support investor outcomes.”

See also: MAS places $1.45 bil with five asset managers; reviewing proposals for a fourth batch of asset managers

To commemorate the milestone, JP Morgan Singapore will make a contribution to SGX Cares Bull Charge, SGX Group’s corporate charity initiative that brings together the financial community to support underprivileged children and families, persons with disabilities and the elderly. The contribution will go towards SGX’s six adopted charities: Autism Association (Singapore), AWWA Limited, Fei Yue Community Services, HCSA Community Services, Shared Services for Charities and Tasek Academy & Social Services.

Ayaz adds that the bank is pleased to mark this achievement by contributing to the SGX Cares Bull Charge, reinforcing its commitment to the broader Singapore community.

title: UOB launches online branch appointment booking system for over 25 services
article:
United Overseas Bank (UOB) has launched its online appointment booking service where its corporate and retail customers can book branch appointments for the next day till 10 days later.

According to UOB, the move to do so marks an industry-first in Singapore and helps its customers reduce transaction times and minimise unnecessary repeat visits.

Appointments can be booked for over 25 services ranging from everyday transactions to advisory and wealth services such as banker’s guarantee applications, cashier’s orders and updates to account particulars.

Customers looking for services that can be performed digitally will be directed to the relevant link at the appointment booking site.

Every branch will have at least two counters dedicated to customers with appointments.

The rollout follows an eight-week pilot conducted across six of the bank’s branches - including in Ang Mo Kio, Anson and Jem - in July and August. During the pilot, customers with appointments were found to have waited an average of seven minutes to be served, compared to the 15-minute wait experienced by walk-in customers. Almost half of all customers who used the appointment booking service were aged 50 years and above. Demand was found to be evenly split between advisory and service-related appointments.

See also: HSBC’s new trading floor has far less headroom than rivals

"Branches remain an important touchpoint for customers seeking advice, guidance and reassurance, whether for their day-to-day banking needs or more complex wealth and financial decisions. As the first bank in Singapore to introduce instant online appointment booking across our branch network, we are making it easier for customers to plan their visits, spend less time waiting and enjoy more dedicated, personalised service,” says Benny Chan, managing director, group channels and digitalisation at UOB.

“The platform also allows us to better anticipate demand and prepare for each interaction, helping us deliver a smoother experience while ensuring our branches continue to play their vital role in serving all customers, especially seniors and those who may be more vulnerable,” he adds.

title: Northern Japanese banks mull merger with US$82 bil in assets
article:
(Oct 2): Three regional lenders in northern Japan agreed to begin talks on a merger that would create the area’s largest banking group, a fresh sign that industry consolidation is gaining momentum as the population declines.

Procrea Holdings Inc, Bank of Iwate Ltd and Akita Bank Ltd, with more than ¥13 trillion (US$82 billion or $106 billion) in total assets, announced the plans in a joint statement following board meetings on Friday, confirming earlier media reports.

They join a growing number of Japanese banks that are considering mergers to survive in an industry facing worsening demographics and an intensifying fight for deposits as interest rates rise. Japan’s financial regulator has been pushing regional lenders to draw up viable long-term visions, including joining operations with rivals.

“Japan’s regional bank consolidation could be entering a faster phase as lenders seek scale against rising competitive and funding pressures,” Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Michael Makdad wrote in a note.

Shares of Procrea, which is the parent company of Aomori Michinoku Bank, rose 5.9% in Tokyo on Friday. Akita Bank closed 0.5% higher and Bank of Iwate was unchanged. Shares of all three lenders have more than doubled this year, giving them a combined market capitalisation of ¥556 billion.

See also: This Japanese tax has a problem: It’s too popular

The three banks are based in the Tohoku region, which has some of the steepest population declines in Japan. A combination would create a banking group with more assets than the area’s biggest lender, 77 Bank Ltd, which is based in Sendai, Miyagi prefecture.

“The operating environment surrounding the three banks is expected to become even more challenging,” the lenders said in the statement. Leveraging their respective strengths will contribute to the sustainable development of their communities and customers and enhance corporate value, they said.

The three banks aim to complete the business integration in April 2028.

See also: Japan to detail first five years of Takaichi investment plan

Asked about the merger plans before the announcement, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said that generally speaking, regional banks are “operating in an increasingly challenging environment, including because of population decline”.

“It’s important that they continue to support their local economies by providing a broad range of financial intermediation services,” she said at a regular briefing. “The Financial Services Agency will continue to encourage regional banks to reform their businesses, whether through mergers and integrations or other means.”

Aomori Michinoku was itself created through a recent consolidation. Two banks in the Aomori prefecture came under the holding company in 2022 before combining into a single lender in 2025.

Japan had 95 regional lenders as of April, according to the Bank of Japan. That’s roughly the equivalent to two in each prefecture. The country is among the most overbanked in the developed world, with about 34 branches per 100,000 people in 2024, higher than 26 in the US and just 16 in Australia, according to World Bank statistics.

Not all mergers have been carried out. San Ju San Financial Group Inc and Aichi Financial Group Inc, based in central Japan, said last month that they scrapped plans to combine, citing differences in views on the business direction.
